doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Basin Street, the airport, statue and the camp's 'keepers of the flame'
summary: Jacobs recalls the club named for Armstrong, praises Harris for the airport name, statue and camp, and says young New Orleans players were inspired by Louis.

venues.name: Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well said. Do you recall in the early — was it at the club that you were working at , was it called —

Basin Street. It was named for Louis Armstrong. That’s what attracted me to Jackie Harris. Not only was she living in the city where Louis was born but she helped us get the airport name for Louis Armstrong, she helped us get the statue in the park, and she has been our representative and part of our Louis Armstrong educational foundation and she’s responsible for some wonderful things that are going on with the camp. And our

camp is, as she’s created, keepers of the flames. They’re the kids that are going out there, now Nicholas Payton or Trombone Shorty, guys like that that come up from New Orleans, they were all inspired by Louis. You can’t do anything in music that Louis hasn’t played.
